keyChanges.title: TSLA -26% in July — worst month since December 2022
keyChanges.description: The Q2 earnings miss (EPS $0.33 vs $0.53 expected, 1.4% op margin, -$1.09B FCF) triggered a month-long selloff from ~$425 to ~$311. Continued analyst note-writing extended the move through late July. Stock is now down ~30% YTD. Market is explicitly repricing Tesla on profit quality failure, not delivery volume. The ~$320 close on July 23 erased >$140B in market cap in a single session, and the bleed continued through month-end.

sentiment.headline: negative
sentiment.rationale: Stock action and analyst coverage uniformly negative post-earnings. No recovery catalyst emerged in the two weeks following the print.

positive_signals: Wedbush maintained $600 Buy — outlier but signals some institutional support
negative_signals: TSLA -26% in July, worst monthly performance since December 2022
Stock down ~30% YTD as of early August
>$140B market cap wiped on July 23 alone
No recovery catalysts emerged through early August
Sustained institutional selling pressure through month-end

key_metrics.actual: TSLA ~$311 end of July; -26% MoM; -30% YTD
key_metrics.target: Market needed margin/profitability proof after Q2 delivery beat
key_metrics.trajectory: Continued downward repricing as auto profit quality fails to match volume headlines

keyChanges.title: Broad analyst price target cuts post-earnings — Hold cluster at $375-400 now institutional consensus
keyChanges.description: No upward PT revisions post-Q2 earnings. Goldman Sachs, Truist, and Morgan Stanley all moved to Hold at ~$375-400. Piper Sandler cut from $500 to $450 on July 28 (stock fell an additional 1.2% that session). Wells Fargo and JPMorgan maintained Underweight at $130-145. Wedbush remained the only notable outlier at $600 Buy. Full-year 2026 EPS consensus cut from ~$1.89 pre-earnings to ~$1.37 post-earnings — a ~28% reduction driven by the operating margin miss and structural loss of regulatory credit revenue.

sentiment.headline: negative
sentiment.rationale: Uniform analyst PT cuts with no upgrades reflects broad institutional consensus that Q2 profit quality was structurally poor, not a one-quarter anomaly.

keyChanges.title: Full-year 2026 delivery consensus revised to ~1.65M — barely 1% growth vs 2025
keyChanges.description: Post-Q2 analyst consensus for full-year 2026 deliveries was cut from ~1.69M to ~1.65M. Q2's 480k beat was inventory-fed (production 28k below deliveries), not a demand re-acceleration. Musk's 20-30% growth guidance — implying ~1.9-2.0M deliveries — is now widely viewed as unreachable by Street consensus. Q3 2026 IR delivery consensus had not yet been published as of August 6. The ~1.65M full-year estimate implies H2 run-rate roughly flat with H1, with no major model refresh or new market entry expected to accelerate volume.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: Headlines emphasize Q2 delivery beat; underlying reality is full-year consensus implies ~1% YoY growth vs management's 20-30% target — a massive guidance miss in the making.

positive_signals: Q2 480k deliveries technically beat pre-print Street estimates

key_metrics.actual: 2026 consensus ~1.65M deliveries; Q2 480k beat on inventory drawdown
key_metrics.trajectory: Consensus converging to ~flat YoY growth; management guidance gap widening

keyChanges.title: Tesla Semi FSD timeline: 'end of year or early 2027' — explicitly sequenced behind Cybercab
keyChanges.description: On the Q2 earnings call, Musk confirmed FSD for Tesla Semi is targeted for end-2026 or early 2027, but explicitly stated it is deprioritized behind Cybercab commercial deployment and Model 3/Y FSD maturity. The 4680 battery cell yield remains the binding constraint for both Semi and Cybercab production ramp. The Nevada Semi factory (1.7M sq ft, 50k/yr capacity) has been ramping since April 2026. Full-year 2026 Semi deliveries estimated at 5,000-15,000 units. Critical read: this is a commercial trucking FSD story (narrow domain), not consumer autonomy expansion.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Semi FSD headline sounds like progress; reality is it's explicitly sequenced behind Cybercab (itself delayed), constrained by 4680 yield, and targeting a narrow commercial trucking domain.

key_metrics.target: 50k/yr Nevada capacity; FSD for commercial revenue use

keyChanges.title: Tesla Argentina pre-launch: hiring and Supercharger deals underway — vehicle sales not until 2027
keyChanges.description: As of August 3, Tesla posted seven Buenos Aires job listings covering sales, service, and Supercharger operations. A Supercharger deal was signed with YPF (17 sites planned, Phase 1 H2 2026). Vehicles already have Argentine regulatory approval. A country manager was appointed in June 2026. The EV market in Argentina grew +1,630% YoY in H1 2026, though from a tiny base. Zero 2026 delivery impact — this is infrastructure/commercial setup for a 2027 sales launch. The announcement pattern mirrors Tesla's pre-launch playbooks in prior LatAm markets.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Argentina expansion is real but a 2027 event; zero 2026 delivery or revenue impact. Positive for long-term market optionality, irrelevant to near-term financials.
